name: Intercom
subcategory: help desks, live chat and support knowledge
tagline: Run a small website inbox and knowledge base without recreating Intercom's AI or channel network

pricing.notes: Official Essential monthly seat price before usage add-ons.

tiers.name: Essential
tiers.limits: 1 full-seat minimum; no Lite seats; unlimited live chat, inbound support email, in-app chats, banners and tooltips
tiers.notes: Includes access to Fin, but Fin outcomes are usage-billed separately.

tiers.name: Advanced
tiers.limits: 1 full-seat minimum; 20 Lite seats included; multiple team inboxes, workflows and round-robin assignment

tiers.name: Expert
tiers.limits: 1 full-seat minimum; 50 Lite seats included; SSO, HIPAA support, SLAs and multibrand Messenger/help center
tiers.notes: Annual subscription is published; monthly seat price is also documented, although monthly self-serve is stated only for Essential and Advanced.

tiers.name: Fin AI Agent for another helpdesk
tiers.limits: $0.99 per outcome; no seat fees; minimum monthly commitment such as 50 outcomes
tiers.notes: Sales-assisted standalone Fin plan for an existing helpdesk; no setup, integration or platform fee.

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier (14-day trial, no card; all plan features, Fin and add-ons included during trial)
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual for Essential and Advanced; annual available on all plans; Expert monthly self-serve not stated
pricing.hiddenCosts: Fin costs $0.99 per outcome on top of seats. Pay-as-you-go charges apply to WhatsApp, SMS, bulk email campaigns and Phone. Copilot is $35/agent/month or $29 annual; Proactive Support Plus is $99/month for 500 messages plus overages; the Pro add-on starts at $99/month with 2,000 credits and extra credits at $0.01 each. Premier support/onboarding and custom terms require a contract.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Intercom, run a small website inbox and knowledge base without recreating Intercom's AI or channel network. The hard boundary is messaging infrastructure, ai resolution, product tours, integrations, and enterprise operations, plus channel integrations and support operations.
coreLoopDIY: Receive website messages into a small shared inbox, reply from one place, maintain a knowledge base, and retain searchable history without recreating Intercom's AI or channel network.
whatYouLose: messaging infrastructure, AI resolution, product tours, integrations, and enterprise operations
ongoingBurden: message delivery, webhooks, threading, identity, permissions, attachments, notifications, spam, search, uptime, and retention
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Intercom because support software survives because missing or misrouting one customer message is expensive and every channel behaves differently. The recurring cost buys message delivery, webhooks, threading, identity, permissions, attachments, notifications, spam, search, uptime, and retention, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Chatwoot
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source customer engagement and shared-inbox platform.

alternatives.name: Chatwoot
alternatives.desc: A proper support inbox with chat, email and a help center; free software, billable server chores.

facts.dataFormat: Conversations, contacts and configuration in PostgreSQL; Redis handles jobs and cache; attachments use local disk or configured object storage
facts.gapVsPaid: It is weaker than Intercom in proactive messaging, AI automation, product tours, customer-data segmentation and the breadth of supported channels and integrations.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting requires a VM or Docker, PostgreSQL, Redis, SMTP, persistent or object storage, HTTPS, backups and upgrades

alternatives.name: Live Helper Chat
alternatives.desc: A battle-tested live-chat desk with routing, transcripts and canned replies; the interface has seen some things.

facts.install: Download the packaged archive and run its PHP web installer
facts.dataFormat: Chats and users in MySQL or MariaDB; uploaded files and cached data on the server
facts.gapVsPaid: Its interface and administration are older, and it lacks Intercom's mature outbound messaging, AI, segmentation and integration ecosystem.
facts.setupBlocker: PHP, MySQL or MariaDB, Apache or Nginx, file permissions, cron and mail or realtime configuration

alternatives.name: tawk.to
alternatives.desc: Live chat, tickets and a knowledge base for zero dollars; the little badge is how the arithmetic survives.

facts.install: Hosted signup plus a JavaScript snippet or CMS plugin
facts.engines: tawk.to AI Assist; underlying models are not disclosed
facts.dataFormat: Chats, tickets and contacts live in tawk.to's cloud database until deleted; chat and ticket data can be exported
facts.gapVsPaid: It offers less sophisticated automation, segmentation, outbound messaging and integration depth than Intercom, and free widgets retain tawk.to branding.
facts.setupBlocker: The website widget or plugin must be installed; removing tawk.to branding is paid

alternatives.name: Zammad
alternatives.desc: A serious ticket desk with email, chat, SLAs and a knowledge base; setup is the first ticket.

facts.install: Hosted signup or Docker Compose, Portainer or OS package
facts.dataFormat: Tickets and users in PostgreSQL, queue and cache in Redis, search in Elasticsearch or OpenSearch, and attachments in filesystem or object storage
facts.gapVsPaid: It is fundamentally a ticketing system, not Intercom's polished website messenger, outbound engagement and AI-support platform.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting normally means Docker plus PostgreSQL, Redis, Elasticsearch or OpenSearch, mail channels, a domain and backups

alternatives.name: Odoo Helpdesk One App Free
alternatives.desc: A real hosted ticket desk for unlimited users, as long as Helpdesk is your one free Odoo app.

facts.dataFormat: Tickets, messages and attachments live in Odoo Online's managed database and filestore
facts.gapVsPaid: It supplies a ticket desk but not Intercom's website messenger, proactive campaigns, product tours, AI layer or channel network.
facts.setupBlocker: None for Helpdesk alone; installing another Odoo app ends the one-app-free arrangement

rejectedAlternatives.name: Chaskiq
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Source is available, but open abandonment and broken-production reports make it a bad non-builder recommendation.

rejectedAlternatives.name: HubSpot Free Help Desk
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The inbox and widget are free; the knowledge base required by this row is not.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Papercups
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The famous open-source Intercom alternative has not seen a main-repo commit since February 2024.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Essential plan and a small-team shared inbox DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Intercom in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, WebSockets, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: receive website messages into a small shared inbox, reply from one place, maintain a knowledge base, and retain searchable history without recreating Intercom's AI or channel network.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement one workspace, agents, contacts, inboxes, conversations, messages, labels, and assignment.
Provide a website chat widget with reconnect, unread counts, file limits, and clear availability state.
Create a shared inbox with filters, collision warnings, notes, canned replies, and searchable history.
Add email notifications, browser notifications, and an immutable assignment and status log.
Implement spam controls, attachment scanning hooks, retention settings, export, and contact deletion.
Ship Docker Compose, backups, health checks, migrations, and a documented admin recovery flow.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out many social and messaging channels.
Deliberately leave out AI agents trained on proprietary support data.
Deliberately leave out enterprise workforce management, SSO, and compliance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
